full_judgment:
16. Muhammad Muzaffar Khan vs Muhammad Yusuf Khan, 11 DLR (SC) 76 arose out of two suits for preemption. Khatian No. 324 of a village in the District of DI Khan, comprising of 54 Khasras and measuring 2664 kanals 1 maria in area were jointly owned and possessed by two brothers, Samundar and Qalandar in equal shares, and the rest half belonged to Alamgir Khan. Muhammad Muzaffar Khan, the appellant, purchased 480 kanals of different khasras of the khata from said Alamgir Khan. No partition was ever effected. Co-sharers possessed in severalty specific shares. Samundar and Qalandr jointly sold 62 kanals to respondent Muhammad Yusuf Khan. A mutation followed. Subsequently, Samundar sold another 30 kanals to said Yusuf Khan. The appellant instituted the suits for preemption of these two sales as co-sharer. 

 Upon such finding, the Supreme Court of Pakistan restored the decision of first two Courts allowing preemption. What Khata, khasras, kanals etc, means, we could not ascertain. Nor we could ascertain the land law in Peshawar at the time. Unlike our land tenure, the land laws there, particularly, in the then West Pakistan was tilted a bit to big land holdings, Besides, unless the law for preemption in Peshawar is not in pari-materia with our law, i.e. the Act, 1949, in brief, the Act, 1949, it is very difficult for us to follow the opinion of the Pakistan Supreme Court. Moreover, if we take Khata meaning a tenancy or holding, the above view of the Supreme Court of Pakistan will be of no help because sections 116 and 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have provided procedure for amalgamation and subdivision of a tenancy or holding, and after a valid subdivision of a holding and distribution of the rents, preemption at the instance of a co-sharer of the former joint holding is not maintainable. 

 "The principle of law on this subject is that where an under-raiyati is created by a raiyat, the latter is not a co-sharer of the former; and when the superior interest of the raiyat is extinguished and he disappears, the under-raiyat is upgraded into a raiyat but only in respect of his own share. If the previous raiyat or for that matter his co-sharer raiyat held khas any portion of the original tenancy, that portion becomes a separate raiyati under the Government with which the upgraded raiyat has got no connection. In view of the position, the under-raiyati held by Ayesha upgraded into an independent raiyati which got no connection with the raiyati previously held by Nafisa, now by respondent No.1 As such, respondent No.1 is not a co-sharer of the appellant and he got no right to pre-empt the land purchased by the appellant from Ayesha Khatun."
